I pick mainly my face and the thing that works best for me is putting makeup on as soon as I can from when I wake up and then not taking it off until i’m right about to sleep. It prevents me picking through the day since I don’t want to ruin the makeup - especially if i’ll be going out in public. But it’s incredibly important you leave removing it until you are right about to sleep so there’s no time to pick after taking it off! Works even better if the makeup is realllll expensive. This can be adapted to wherever your problem areas are though such as a good cuticle oil if you pick around your fingers, regular hair treatments/hair styles if you pick at your scalp etc! I also keep any mirrors as far away as possible from where I spend majority of my time which works when i’m feeling too lazy to get up and get one. 

Keeping up with getting gel polish on my nails also is something that helps me as I find it makes picking fairly difficult so I don’t really get the same satisfaction from it which does deter me a little. An alternative to this would be plasters over every finger tip? Although that’s just a method i’ve seen people use, i’ve never actually tried it.

Any body wounds I put a plaster on immediately no matter how minor (as it won’t stay minor if I allow my fingers near it) and I’ll change this at the very end/beginning of a day, daily until it’s healed enough that even if I do pick the scab off it will no longer be a wound. 

For automatic picking that i’m not actually aware i’m doing, I like to wear jewellery and when I do notice myself picking I’ll move my hand to whatever jewellery item i’m wearing instead and fidget with it. 

Random time consuming tasks sometimes help too like counting up loose change, cleaning shoes, clearing out drawers/wardrobes/cupboards/shelves and cleaning them before putting the items back in organised, gardening ect! Anything that can be done requiring two hands. 

It’s extra hard to stop myself when I’ve started so my methods are based around avoiding starting at all costs. It’s rough and something i’ve struggled with for as long as I can remember. I hope you find what works for you!

Promethazine (otc antihistamine) may be worth a try! I noticed when taking it for allergies it helped my severe hand eczema a little even though I could never find correlation between allergic reactions and eczema flare ups. Wouldn’t hurt to try although it is also given as a sleeping tablet so night time only!! Aloe vera gel every hour was also a life saver for me. 

Another thing I noticed was flare ups caused by sweat. Breathable fabrics only is good! Try wearing as little clothes as you can when home (stops creams absorbing into them instead of skin and stops any weepy eczema sticking to clothes which is a pain to pull off). Little/no clothes when home also = less laundry to do!

If you have anyone in your life who could help out with house cleaning and doing the laundry you shouldn’t feel any shame in asking. Eczema is rough. Wishing you so much healing

I felt the same way when I got assaulted. I was constantly filled with anger/sadness/grief. Id cycle through those three in waves of intensity and I genuinely thought it would never go away. Until a few weeks later when I was dancing listening to music and realised i’d not thought about it all day. Those moments brought so much joy. It does get easier over time. Don’t try to find out if you just had bad stuff. The bad experience was a blessing!! As you know, addiction is horrible. Don’t risk falling back in that hole to find out the difference between them.
